result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B uses all 14 real toggles in clear sections and puts the two master switches and quiet hours at the top as a separate block. It also shows the difference between garden care and marketing through section order and off-by-default marketing toggles. A's Push/Email grid adds per-channel switches that don't exist in the request, so the number of controls goes up even though it has fewer rows. B's one-item 'Summaries & News' section is a little awkward, and B never says which sections start collapsed. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A sorts all 14 real toggles into clear sections, puts both master switches and quiet hours at the top, and shows marketing as off by default in a layout you could build as drawn. B adds a push/email grid that invents channel options for each topic and creates more switches than the original list. It also says this cuts the screen to about 8 rows, but its own layout still has about 12. B does say plainly what is collapsed and what the defaults are, but its redesign goes beyond the request and could make the screen busier, not simpler.
